rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The essay at a glance "How to Live Before You Die" is the title under which NEB anthologises Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford commencement address — and the title is the speech's thesis in five words. rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Three stories: dots (trust the future), love (do what you love), death (live each day fully).
'Stay hungry, stay foolish' — memorise this closing for theme questions.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The 'dots' metaphor: you can only connect them looking BACKWARDS, so trust in the future — the most-quoted line; use it in theme answers.  ·  ## The themes worth an essay **Trust in the unplanned** — the dots theme: meaning is visible only backward, so curiosity must lead where calculation cannot. **Love your work** — the career theme, argued as necessity rather than luxury: satisfaction comes only from work you believe in.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The title, defended "How to Live Before You Die" inverts the usual graduation cliché — advice for the future — into advice for the present, and the inversion is the speech's whole stance. The defence: the title announces death as the deadline that gives life its urgency, and every story in the speech obeys it — the dropout, the fired founder and the cancer patient all act *now* because the time is limited.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why did Jobs drop out of college, and what did he do after? (2 marks)** A. He saw no value in it — it was spending his parents' savings — so he dropped out and stayed on auditing the classes that interested him, including calligraphy. The apparent detour later shaped the Macintosh's beautiful typography. **Q. What does "connecting the dots" mean? (2 marks)** A.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. What are the three stories Jobs tells? (3 marks) — connecting the dots; love and loss; death.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. Narrate the three stories Jobs tells and draw out the lesson of each. (8 marks)** A model answer retells each story in two sentences and closes each with its lesson: the dropout whose calligraphy class returned as typography — trust the dots to connect; the founder fired at thirty whose exile produced NeXT, Pixar and his return — love your work and keep looking until you find it; the…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The argument, step by step **Story one: connecting the dots.** Jobs explains his adoption, his six months at Reed College and his eighteen more dropping in on classes he liked — including calligraphy, a course with no practical use. Ten years later that knowledge returned as the Mac's typography.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Anecdote structure** — the speech's architecture: three personal stories, each ending in a portable lesson; the exam question on structure is answered by naming the three-story plan. - **Refrain** — "Stay hungry, stay foolish" opens and closes the address, borrowed from The Whole Earth Catalog: the speech's takeaway sentence, engineered for memorability.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Three stories = three lessons: connecting dots (trust that experiences connect), love and loss (do what you love), death (live each day as your last) — structure every answer around the three.  ·  Trick 2: 'Stay hungry, stay foolish' — the closing motto; explain what each half means (never complacent; take risks).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What does 'stay hungry, stay foolish' mean? (2 marks) — keep ambition and curiosity alive; dare to take risks.
